# PR-head review threads: acme/widget#82

## Setup and query owner

**Aliases**

| Alias | Value |
|---|---|
| ROOT | `/work/widget` |
| W | `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` (clean, on `fix/retry` at H) |
| H | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` (headRefOid, `aaaaaaa`) |
| B | `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (origin/main, `bbbbbbb`) |

**Query owner.** `reference/pr-head.md` § "Fetch unresolved review threads" owns both queries, so they are not copied here.

- Q1 is the paginated `reviewThreads` query.
- Q2 is the per-thread comment follow-up, keyed by thread id with its own comment cursor.

This step runs for every admitted PR, N=1 included, before gather. The process cwd never changes. Both queries pass owner, repo and number explicitly, so they do not depend on cwd.

**Commands**

| # | Command | cwd |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<Q1>' -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | unchanged process cwd |
| C2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query='<Q2>' -F id=<T1 id>` | unchanged process cwd |

## Successful fetch

**Merge and filter.** C1 returns three `reviewThreads` pages, which are merged and then filtered to `isResolved == false`.

| Page | Thread | isResolved | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T1 | false | yes |
| 2 | T2 | false (outdated) | yes |
| 2 | TX `src/gone.ts:2` | true | **dropped** |
| 3 | T3 | false | yes |

**T1 comment pagination.** T1's comments report `hasNextPage: true` and `totalCount=102`, so the first page does not hold them all.

- C2 runs from T1's first comment page to its last page.
- Comment page 1 holds 100 comments: the original plus replies 1–99.
- Comment page 2 holds replies 100–101.
- C2's full connection of 102 comments replaces T1's initial 100, so there are no duplicates.
- The comment cursor stays separate from the reviewThreads cursor.

T2 and T3 report no further comment pages, so they need no follow-up.

**Location rule.**

- Use `<path>:<line>` when `line` is set.
- Otherwise use `<path>:<originalLine> (outdated)`.
- Otherwise use `<path>` alone.

Every comment carries the same metadata: url `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`, author `reviewer`, createdAt `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Comments are listed in their original order.

**Rendered threads (input to gather)**

**T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`**

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Rewrite the retry engine |
| 2–101 (replies 1–100) | Rewrite still requested |
| 102 (reply 101) | Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines. |

- **Effective request:** keep the existing engine and cap retries in a two-line change.
- **Superseded request:** the original "rewrite the retry engine" is overridden by the final reply.
- This correction is visible only because every page was read. Truncating at 100 comments would have carried a stale rewrite request into the spec.

**T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`**

`line` is null and `originalLine` is 7, so the outdated form applies.

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Keep this guard |
| 2 | Yes, retain it |

- **Effective request:** retain the guard. The reply confirms it.

**T3 — `README.md`**

Both `line` and `originalLine` are null, so only the path is shown.

| # | Body |
|---|---|
| 1 | Document the cap |

- **Effective request:** document the retry cap in the README.

**Outcome:** 3 unresolved threads (T1, T2, T3) are carried to gather. Gather and the spec follow.

## Failed fetch (independent case)

C1 fails with `API unavailable`. A failure on a C2 comment fetch would be treated the same way.

The per-PR stop applies even in this N=1 run:

> `threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)`

The run stops **before gather and the spec**:

- no draft is written and no Rework record is made;
- no thread list is assumed empty, so there is no silent continuation.

Finish's separate post-verification fetch-failure reporting does not apply at this point.

## Empty set (independent case)

C1 succeeds and, after filtering, there are zero unresolved threads.

Record: `Threads: none`

Gather proceeds with no review-thread inputs.

I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

This narration covers **only review-thread fetching**, as requested. Provisioning, base merge, and the Step 4 workspace report are outside this scope.

### Command and query legend

All commands below run with **cwd `/work/widget`**; no cwd changes occur.

Resolved values: `ROOT=/work/widget`, `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, owner=`acme`, repository=`widget`, PR=`82`.

The query and pagination owner is **`using-git-worktrees/reference/pr-head.md`, “Fetch unresolved review threads.”**

- `$QT` denotes that section’s exact, unmodified **reviewThreads query**.
- `$QC` denotes its exact, unmodified **thread-comments query**.

These symbols identify the literal query arguments without reproducing the queries. No tools or tracker calls are actually executed here.

### Independent successful fetch

| Order | Command, with exact remaining arguments | Result / resolved values |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82` | Fetch all three reviewThreads pages, using the connection’s returned `endCursor` as `endCursor` for each next page. Merge pages; retain unresolved T1, T2, T3; exclude resolved TX. |
| 2 | `gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QC" -F id=T1` | Start T1’s comments at its first page and paginate using its own comment cursor, separate from the reviewThreads cursor. Fetch all 102 comments; replace—not append to—the initial partial connection. |

T1’s `totalCount=102` and initial `hasNextPage=true` require command 2. With the query’s `first:100`, its complete comment pages contain: first comment plus replies 1–99, then replies 100–101. Pagination ends only after the final comment page.

**Rendering legend:** Every comment below individually carries:
- URL: `https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/82#discussion_r1`
- Author: `reviewer`
- createdAt: `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`

Ranges below represent distinct consecutive comments, each retaining that metadata—not a deduplicated comment.

| Thread / rendered location | Complete ordered comments |
|---|---|
| **T1 — `src/retry.ts:12`** | **1:** “Rewrite the retry engine” → **2–101 (replies 1–100, individually):** “Rewrite still requested” → **102 (reply 101):** “Correction: keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.” |
| **T2 — `src/old.ts:7 (outdated)`** | **1:** “Keep this guard” → **2:** “Yes, retain it” |
| **T3 — `README.md`** | **1:** “Document the cap” |

**Resulting repair requests carried to gather:**
- T1: **Keep the engine; cap retries in two lines.** The final correction supersedes the original rewrite request despite the intervening 100 replies.
- T2: Retain the guard; preserve the outdated-location annotation.
- T3: Document the cap.

TX at `src/gone.ts:2` is resolved and is not carried forward. The successful fetch supplies all unresolved threads and their complete ordered comments to gather.

### Independent failed fetch

Starting independently after successful provisioning:

```bash
gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82
```

Cwd: `/work/widget`. Fetch fails with `API unavailable`.

**Stop immediately, including for this N=1 run:**

```text
threads for #82 not fetched (API unavailable)
```

No gather, spec, draft, or continuation record follows.

### Independent successful empty fetch

Starting independently after successful provisioning:

```bash
gh api graphql --paginate -f query="$QT" -F o=acme -F r=widget -F n=82
```

Cwd: `/work/widget`. Successful complete pagination yields no unresolved threads. No comment-pagination command is needed.

Record:

```text
Threads: none
```

Two After wording slips are worth tightening so the threads fact stays unambiguous: After describes Q2 only as 'keyed by thread id' and never names the `node(id:)` mechanism that Before stated explicitly (keep one phrase like 'Q2 uses node(id:) on T1's id with its own comment cursor'), and the sentence 'Both queries pass owner, repo and number explicitly' is wrong for Q2, which passes only the thread id per C2 — say 'Q1 passes owner/repo/number; Q2 passes the thread id' instead. The Change itself concerns provisioning/rebase behavior and does not touch this thread-fetch narration, so the After text can carry it without affecting either fact.
